results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 63 aligned outline summaries match the controlling idea of their aligned spec paragraph, in spec order (p01-p45, p49-p50, p46-p48, p51-p63, matching the spec's section order with Vertical Differences before Trade-offs). The five callout units are opening callouts (KEY POINTS, IN THIS CHAPTER, etc.) with no spec paragraph and add no stray controlling idea.

results.draft_locus: Capability, Value Stream, Product, System ¶7
results.quote: That is also why only the map answers Ingrid's question: an inventory of 412 applications cannot say how many do the same job.
results.finding: The outliner marked this unit as two ideas: capability-organized software and Conway's law, and why only the map answers Ingrid's question. The second does not follow from the first (Lewis, Fowler and Conway say nothing about what an inventory can count). The spec's controlling idea for p14 itself joins the two ideas with 'which is also why', so the draft faithfully carries a compound controlling idea; the fix is to move the Ingrid sentence to the end of p13 (the comparable property) or give it its own unit.

Every unit traces to a supporting claim: scene and terms to C1, map to C2, value streams to C3, heat map and public record to C4, worked example to C5, vertical differences to C2/C4, trade-offs, failure modes, Chief Architect's view and questions to C6/C4, conclusion to the thesis claim and so-what. The callouts restate the thesis and the failure patterns.

results.draft_locus: Value Streams: Where Capabilities Meet Outcomes ¶2
results.quote: Figure 4 draws list-to-sell for the Rotterdam city bike, with the timings from that Sunday evening.
results.finding: The prose says the figure carries the timings from that Sunday evening, but the figure (and its caption, per both flow readers) includes the Ghost Inventory hand-off, which happens on Monday (sold 18:10, removed 18:11) and in the next morning's digest. Prose and figure disagree on what the figure shows.

results.draft_locus: Veldmark Worked Example: Five Overlaps, One Commercial Clash, One Deliberate Duplicate ¶2
results.quote: Keybridge multi-diffusion
results.finding: The heat-map table has a row 'Feed and bulk ingestion; listing distribution | 2 (Hearthly ingestion, Keybridge multi-diffusion)' (quoted by both flow readers). 'Listing distribution' is not among the capabilities the chapter names and 'multi-diffusion' is never explained; the prose legend explains only the T/M/H/K abbreviations. The row is the deliberate-duplicate evidence, so its terms should be explained or replaced with the prose's own words ('Keybridge's listing distribution').

All other evidence is introduced and interpreted in the prose: the TOGAF paraphrase, OMG and Wikipedia quotations, Lewis and Fowler and Conway quotations, the term table, Figures 1-3 and 5, the level-2 and level-3 tables, the stream and bottleneck tables (bold cells explained in p27), the maturity scale and verdict table, the DDD Crew quotation, the Adevinta, Rightmove, Autotrader and Vinted sources (each followed by the lesson drawn), the 88/nine reference-model statistics, the vertical table and the trade-off table (p47 refers to its rows). No other contradictions found.

results.draft_locus: Trade-offs: Ways to Build a Capability Map ¶1
results.quote: A group building its own map has four common starting points, and the choice shapes what the map can and cannot answer.
results.finding: Declared: sequence, carrying 'the finished Veldmark map and its vertical weightings' into 'the choices behind building any map'. The opening sentence makes no reference to the finished map or the vertical section; it starts a new topic cold. Both flow readers found this section's position only partly clear because the worked example had already shown the method. A sentence that turns from the finished Veldmark map to the choices behind building any map would express the declared sequence.

All other transitions express their declared relationship at the boundary: introduction (sequence, example), scene (problem_solution via the heading's question; contrast, example, conclusion_summary), terms (elaboration, sequence x4, cause_effect x2), map (sequence, elaboration x2, sequence, example, cause_effect, additional_support, conclusion_summary), value streams (cause_effect, example, cause_effect, additional_support, elaboration, contrast), heat map (sequence, sequence x3, cause_effect, emphasis 'The last row is the one maps forget', contrast), public record (example, example, contrast, additional_support x2), worked example (contrast 'Unlike the public record', sequence, cause_effect, additional_support, conclusion_summary), verticals (elaboration, example), trade-offs p47/p48, failure modes (contrast, similarity, sequence x6), Chief Architect (problem_solution 'Those failures are mostly governance failures'), questions (conclusion_summary phrase), conclusion (conclusion_summary, contrast).

Post level: both flow readers describe the organising principle as building a tool one layer at a time and then using it (question -> vocabulary -> map -> value streams -> scores -> outside evidence -> worked case -> vertical explanation -> method choices, failures, governance, questions -> hand-off), which agrees with the declared prerequisite_order with assertion_evidence_reasoning for evidence and grouping for the closing sections. Reader B: 'On the whole the order is easy to see.' No section is marked plainly unclear. Points judged not material because audience.already_knows covers them (preface: Veldmark's four brands, cast, the fifteen failure-pattern names): Keybridge as a brand (A1, B9), Tradeyard's country units (A7, A8, B10, B18), the 'Ghost Inventory' pattern name (A2, B1, as a name), plus minor single-reader points (Veldmark ID explained in the next paragraph A9, pronoun 'it' B12, term drift B19).

results.draft_locus: Trade-offs: Ways to Build a Capability Map ¶1
results.quote: A group building its own map has four common starting points, and the choice shapes what the map can and cannot answer.

The conclusion synthesises the three instruments into one answer and hands off with a contrast to bounded contexts; no plain recap, no new material, no generic moral.

p62 answers 'what do we pay for four times?' with a verdict per capability that needs map, value streams and scores together, lists Veldmark's verdicts (two consolidations, three splits, one commercial clash, one kept duplicate), and states the so-what: the Chief Architect can defend Common Ground's order with evidence and say which overlaps are not platform questions.
p62 opens with Henrik de Boer's question and recalls the Rotterdam bike needing the same capabilities in every brand, as the spec's callback requires; p63 hands off to bounded contexts.

The cold reader of the opening predicted all sections in the actual order: Veldmark's four-times question, the four terms, the three-level map with ten areas, four value streams, heat-map on three scores without merging every duplicate (with level-3 splitting), the public record, Veldmark's five overlaps, commercial clash and deliberate duplicate, vertical differences, ways to build a map, failure modes, the Chief Architect's view and questions; scope edges (decomposition, vertical requirements, consolidation left to later chapters); evidence as fictional Veldmark plus public-record sources.
